title: Getting started with gq
text: gq ships real data Bittner Creek near Prince George, ~40 km² watershed: boundary, streams lakes BC Freshwater Atlas, roads Digital Road Atlas, railway PSCIS fish passage assessments BC Data Catalogue.
code: library(sf) #> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE sf_use_s2(FALSE) #> Spherical geometry (s2) switched off  data(bittner_wsd, bittner_streams, bittner_lakes,      bittner_roads, bittner_railway, bittner_pscis, neexdzii_bc,      package = "gq")  # The assessments are bundled for the watershed's bounding box widened by # 2 km, so some fall outside the watershed. The map is about Bittner Creek, so it shows the ones inside # rather than framing the watershed while symbols sit beyond it (gq#62). pscis_aoi <- bittner_pscis[lengths(st_intersects(bittner_pscis, bittner_wsd)) > 0, ] #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersects assumes that they #> are planar #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersects assumes that they #> are planar  cat("Watershed:", round(bittner_wsd$area_ha), "ha\n") #> Watershed: 4008 ha cat("PSCIS crossings:", nrow(bittner_pscis), "bundled,", nrow(pscis_aoi),     "inside the watershed\n") #> PSCIS crossings: 23 bundled, 10 inside the watershed

what: tmap: a static map for reports
title: Getting started with gq
text: gq_tmap_style(reg, "name") returns tmap arguments layer, layer drawn .call(). Classified layers come categorical scale, field names column data calls something registry . PSCIS fish passage assessments Bittner Creek watershed, classified barrier status. crossings, roads lakes drawn straight gq registry, streams railway take colours . crossings, roads lakes map drawn straight registry, streams railway take colours , match QGIS project field crews use: red barrier, green passable, orange potential barrier purple unknown values QGIS draws. watershed outline, shading outside railway’s white dashes set hand, registry entry first two model dashes yet.
code: library(tmap) #> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'stars': #>   method                  from #>   st_interpolate_aw.stars sf  # Pad the watershed's bbox to the canvas aspect so the map fills the page. bbox <- gq_bbox_aspect(bittner_wsd, asp = 7 / 6)  canvas <- gq_basemap_tiles(bbox, provider = "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",                            zoom = 12, pad = 0, crs = NULL) relief <- gq_basemap_tiles(bbox, provider = "Esri.WorldShadedRelief",                            zoom = 12, pad = 0, crs = NULL)  # gq_basemap_tiles() returns NULL when a fetch fails, so build the whole layer # conditionally: tm_shape() rejects NULL. The tile credit travels with the # raster as an attribute; no tiles drawn, no credit owed. credit <- NULL basemap <- if (is.null(canvas) || is.null(relief)) {   NULL } else {   blended <- gq_basemap_blend(canvas, relief, method = "gamma", gamma = 0.5)   credit <- attr(blended, "credit")   tm_shape(blended) + tm_rgb() }  # Keep only what reaches the frame. gq_bbox_clip() returns NULL rather than an # empty layer, which tm_shape() would reject. roads <- gq_bbox_clip(bittner_roads, bbox) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersects assumes that they #> are planar railway <- gq_bbox_clip(bittner_railway, bbox) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersects assumes that they #> are planar streams <- gq_bbox_clip(bittner_streams[bittner_streams$stream_order >= 3, ], bbox) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersects assumes that they #> are planar  # One label per named stream, from order 4 up named <- bittner_streams[!is.na(bittner_streams$gnis_name) &                            bittner_streams$stream_order >= 4, ] stream_labels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(named, named$gnis_name), function(x) {   st_sf(gnis_name = x$gnis_name[1],         geometry = st_point_on_surface(st_union(x)), crs = st_crs(x)) })) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_union assumes that they are #> planar #> Warning in st_point_on_surface.sfc(st_union(x)): st_point_on_surface may not #> give correct results for longitude/latitude data stream_sty <- gq_style(reg, "streams_all") railway_sty <- gq_style(reg, "railway") label_sty <- gq_style(reg, "stream_labels")$label # The stream class every bundled segment is drawn as: the data carries no # feature code, so one class stands for them all, and the legend says so. stream_key <- names(stream_sty$classification$values)[[1]]  # Knock back everything outside the watershed so the subject reads at a glance. bb_box <- st_as_sfc(bbox, crs = st_crs(bittner_wsd)) aoi_mask <- st_difference(bb_box, st_geometry(bittner_wsd)) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_difference assumes that they #> are planar  m <- basemap + tm_shape(bb_box) +   tm_borders(lwd = 0, col = NA) + tm_shape(aoi_mask) +   tm_polygons(fill = "white", fill_alpha = 0.45, col = NA, lwd = 0) + tm_shape(bittner_wsd) +   tm_polygons(fill_alpha = 0, col = "#2c3e50", lwd = 1.5)  if (!is.null(streams)) {   m <- m + tm_shape(streams) +     tm_lines(col = stream_sty$classification$values[[stream_key]],              lwd = stream_sty$classification$widths[[stream_key]] * 3) } m <- m + tm_shape(bittner_lakes) +   do.call(tm_polygons, gq_tmap_style(reg, "lake")) if (!is.null(roads)) {   m <- m + tm_shape(roads) +     do.call(tm_lines, gq_tmap_style(reg, "roads_dra", field = "road_type")) } # Railway: the registry carries the black line; the white dashed overlay QGIS # draws on it is a second symbol layer the registry does not model yet. if (!is.null(railway)) {   m <- m + tm_shape(railway) +     tm_lines(col = railway_sty$stroke$color,              lwd = railway_sty$stroke$width * 3) +   tm_shape(railway) +     tm_lines(col = "white", lwd = railway_sty$stroke$width * 1.5, lty = "42") } m <- m + tm_shape(pscis_aoi) +   do.call(tm_dots, gq_tmap_style(reg, "crossings_pscis_assessment")) + tm_shape(stream_labels) +   tm_text("gnis_name", size = 0.6, col = label_sty$color, fontface = "italic",           options = opt_tm_text(shadow = TRUE, remove_overlap = TRUE))  # The legend is built from the registry, cut to the classes the frame shows. leg <- gq_tmap_legend(   reg,   c("Lake" = "lake", "Stream" = "streams_all", "roads_dra",     "Railway" = "railway", "crossings_pscis_assessment"),   present = list(     streams_all = stream_key,     roads_dra = if (is.null(roads)) character(0) else unique(roads$road_type),     crossings_pscis_assessment = unique(pscis_aoi$barrier_result_code)   ) ) m <- Reduce(`+`, c(list(m), lapply(leg, function(x) do.call(tm_add_legend, x))))  # Four corners, one element each: legend bottom-left, scale bar top-left, # keymap top-right, logo bottom-right. The keymap took the bottom-right corner # first and covered two crossings on the watershed's south-east edge; the # north-east is empty ground, and the small logo fits beyond the boundary. m <- m + tm_scalebar(   breaks = gq_scale_breaks(st_bbox(st_transform(bb_box, 3005))),   text.size = 0.7, position = c("left", "top"), margins = c(0, 0, 0, 0) ) + tm_logo(system.file("logo", "nge_icon_200.png", package = "gq"),         position = c("right", "bottom"), height = 2.5, margins = c(0, 0, 0, 0)) + tm_layout(   frame = TRUE, frame.lwd = 0.5, asp = 0,   legend.position = c("left", "bottom"),   legend.frame = TRUE, legend.bg.color = "white", legend.bg.alpha = 0.85,   # Sized for the ~700 px column the figure is published in, not for the   # 7 in render.   legend.text.size = 0.7, legend.title.size = 0.8,   inner.margins = rep(0.001, 4), outer.margins = rep(0.003, 4),   meta.margins = 0 )  # The tile credit goes below the frame, since the four corners are taken. The # map prints into a viewport above a fixed strip, so it keeps its 7:6 canvas # (the figure is 6.25 in tall for that) and the keymap nests inside it. strip <- grid::unit(0.25, "inches") map_vp <- grid::viewport(y = 1, just = "top",                          height = grid::unit(1, "npc") - strip) print(m, vp = map_vp) if (!is.null(credit)) {   grid::grid.text(credit, x = grid::unit(0.004, "npc"), y = strip * 0.5,                   just = "left", gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 7, col = "grey30")) } km <- gq_tmap_keymap(bittner_wsd, neexdzii_bc, reg = reg, asp = 7 / 6,                      corner = "topright") grid::pushViewport(map_vp) print(km$map, vp = km$viewport) grid::popViewport()

title: Map composition with gq and tmap
text: muted raster basemap gives terrain relief without competing labels. sub-watershed scale gray canvas blended hillshade works well. Note zoom. Esri.WorldGrayCanvas carries faint place labels , appear zoom — zoom = 10 area none visible, zoom = 12 lake names . raise zoom, check basemap competing labels place . Pick keyless provider deliberately. vignette used Carto’s Positron Carto made basemaps key-began serving “API KEY REQUIRED” watermark instead — valid image, nothing errored watermarked map shipped published site (gq#57).
code: # Pad the bbox to the canvas aspect ratio (7:9) so the map fills the page. The # latitude correction a geographic CRS needs is applied from the CRS rather # than by hand -- this data is lat/lon, so it fires here and would not in BC # Albers. bbox <- gq_bbox_aspect(neexdzii_wsd, asp = 7 / 9)  canvas <- gq_basemap_tiles(bbox, provider = "Esri.WorldGrayCanvas",                            zoom = 10, pad = 0, crs = NULL) relief <- gq_basemap_tiles(bbox, provider = "Esri.WorldShadedRelief",                            zoom = 10, pad = 0, crs = NULL)  # gq_basemap_tiles() returns NULL on a failed fetch so the caller can draw an # unshaded map rather than lose the figure. Honour that here rather than only # documenting it -- a tile hiccup during a pkgdown build should not fail it. # # Build the whole LAYER conditionally, not just the data. tm_shape() rejects # NULL outright ("not a recognized/supported spatial data class"), so setting # the stars object to NULL and passing it on only moves the failure sixty lines # down -- the guard reads as if it works and does not. `NULL + tm_shape(...)` # composes fine, so an absent layer is the shape that actually holds. # The tile providers' terms require attribution, and a blend owes both # (gq#58). It is drawn below the frame when the map is printed; NULL here means # no tiles were drawn, so no credit is owed. credit <- NULL basemap <- if (is.null(canvas) || is.null(relief)) {   NULL } else {   # A relief tile service spans the full range, so the gamma operator suits it.   # A hillshade derived from a DEM is far more contrasty and wants   # `method = "weight"`, which caps how much brightness can be removed.   blended <- gq_basemap_blend(canvas, relief, method = "gamma", gamma = 0.5)   credit <- attr(blended, "credit")   tm_shape(blended) + tm_rgb() }  # Now that the frame is known, drop anything outside it. gq_bbox_clip() returns # NULL rather than a zero-row object, which is what tm_shape() needs -- it # errors on an empty geometry set instead of skipping it. streams_display <- gq_bbox_clip(streams_display, bbox) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_intersects assumes that they #> are planar

title: Map composition with gq and tmap
text: Draw order matters: polygons first, habitat lines, base streams, lakes top, transport, point features (crossings, fish, falls), labels last. Neexdzii Kwa subbasin: salmon habitat classified use barrier status, assessed PSCIS crossing inventory. Habitat, crossings, fish observations, falls, roads, lakes wetlands drawn gq registry. Every registry layer map traces back gq_reg_main(); watershed outline, shading outside label colour set hand: Simple layers (lake, wetland) use gq_tmap_style(reg, "name") directly. Streams railway drawn hand needs something registry model — one class pulled classified layer, white casing black line Classified layers (crossings, roads, habitat) use .call() gq_tmap_style() — classification field, colors, labels, line widths dashes come registry. Labels follow classes data actually carries: registry’s 26 road classes matched handful present rather recycled positionally (#53). Every aesthetic mapped per class, salmon habitat draws spawning, rearing access reaches three registry widths intermittent reaches dashed — mapping_code layers encode habitat use width barrier status colour, axes render (#36) legend built gq_tmap_legend() registry — partitions geometry type, expands classified layers, collapses classes render identically, cuts classified layer classes present data. Change colour registry every element updates Reading habitat lines. Width habitat use — spawning widest, accessible-thinnest — colour barrier status downstream. dashed line width colour intermittent reach. legend lists solid variants : dashed class differs solid twin dash alone, showing double habitat entries explain one distinction. deliberate narrowing rather something gq_tmap_legend() — dedup keys whole entry including label, classes sharing colour merge .
code: bb_box <- st_as_sfc(bbox, crs = st_crs(neexdzii_wsd)) logo_path <- system.file("logo", "nge_icon_200.png", package = "gq")  tmap_mode("plot") #> ℹ tmap modes "plot" - "view" #> ℹ toggle with `tmap::ttm()`  # Pull styles from registry — all colors trace back to gq_reg_main() stream_sty <- gq_style(reg, "streams_all") railway_sty <- gq_style(reg, "railway") fish_sty <- gq_style(reg, "bcfishobs_fiss_fish_observations") falls_sty <- gq_style(reg, "fiss_obstacles") lake_sty <- gq_style(reg, "lake")  # Polygon layers — do.call() with gq_tmap_style() directly # Contain the AOI. Without this, inside and outside the watershed render # identically and only a thin boundary line separates them, so the subject of # the map is not visually obvious -- a reader has to be told where to look. # Knocking back everything outside does that without hiding the context, which # a hard clip would. # # Note the frame is 41% padding by height, split evenly above and below (7:9 # portrait against a ~1.32:1 landscape watershed). That padding is where the # scalebar, logo, legend and keymap live, so it is element space rather than # waste -- but it only reads that way once the AOI itself stands out. aoi_mask <- sf::st_difference(bb_box, sf::st_geometry(neexdzii_wsd)) #> although coordinates are longitude/latitude, st_difference assumes that they #> are planar  m <- basemap + tm_shape(bb_box) +   tm_borders(lwd = 0, col = NA) + tm_shape(aoi_mask) +   tm_polygons(fill = "white", fill_alpha = 0.45, col = NA, lwd = 0) + tm_shape(neexdzii_wsd) +   tm_polygons(fill_alpha = 0, col = "#2c3e50", lwd = 1.5) + tm_shape(neexdzii_wetlands) +   do.call(tm_polygons, gq_tmap_style(reg, "wetland"))  # Salmon habitat — classified by mapping_code (xref: streams_salmon_vw uses # mapping_code, registry expects mapping_code_salmon from WHSE source) m <- m + tm_shape(neexdzii_habitat) +   do.call(tm_lines, gq_tmap_style(reg, "streams_salmon", field = "mapping_code"))  # Base streams on top of habitat — simple style, width scaled up for display. # gq_bbox_clip() returns NULL when nothing survives the frame, so test for it # rather than handing tm_shape() an empty geometry set — the same guard the # basemap uses above, and the one the file already applies to railway and falls. if (!is.null(streams_display)) {   m <- m +     tm_shape(streams_display) +     tm_lines(col = stream_sty$classification$values[[1]],              lwd = stream_sty$classification$widths[[1]] * 2) } m <- m + tm_shape(neexdzii_lakes) +   do.call(tm_polygons, gq_tmap_style(reg, "lake"))  # Lake labels — color from registry if (nrow(lakes_named) > 0) {   m <- m + tm_shape(lakes_named) +     tm_text("gnis_name_1", size = 0.7, col = lake_sty$stroke$color,             fontface = "italic",             options = opt_tm_text(shadow = TRUE)) }  # Roads — classified by transport_line_type_code, bundled data column is # road_type (xref: alias from data-raw query) m <- m + tm_shape(neexdzii_roads) +   do.call(tm_lines, gq_tmap_style(reg, "roads_dra", field = "road_type"))  # Railway — base + white dashed overlay, colors from registry if (nrow(neexdzii_railway) > 0) {   m <- m + tm_shape(neexdzii_railway) +     tm_lines(col = railway_sty$stroke$color,              lwd = railway_sty$stroke$width * 2) +   tm_shape(neexdzii_railway) +     tm_lines(col = "white", lwd = railway_sty$stroke$width, lty = "42") }  # Crossings — classified by barrier_status (xref: bcfishpass.crossings uses # barrier_status, registry expects barrier_result_code from PSCIS WHSE) # # An editorial decision, and the reason for it: 130 of these 146 crossings are # POTENTIAL -- modelled candidates for assessment rather than surveyed sites. # At their true registry size (3 mm, correct since #16) they are 89% of the # point symbols on the map and they bury the stream network the habitat # classification exists to describe. QGIS never shows this because you would be # zoomed in; a static overview has to choose. # # So this map shows the assessed inventory and says so. The modelled crossings # are not wrong and are not mis-sized -- they are a different map's subject. # Note what is NOT done here: hand-tuning `size` down for one class would # reintroduce exactly the per-map guessing #16 removed. crossings_assessed <- neexdzii_crossings[   neexdzii_crossings$barrier_status != "POTENTIAL", ]  m <- m + tm_shape(crossings_assessed) +   do.call(tm_dots, gq_tmap_style(reg, "crossings_pscis_assessment",                                   field = "barrier_status"))  # Fish observations — colour, size AND shape now all come from the registry. # These two layers hardcoded `size` and `shape` until #16: the registry carries # a mark shape for 15 layers that nothing translated, and its millimetre sizes # converted through a guessed divisor, so every map hand-tuned its own numbers. # `col` is still set to the fill colour to give the symbol a matching edge. if (nrow(neexdzii_fish_obs) > 0) {   fish_args <- gq_tmap_style(reg, "bcfishobs_fiss_fish_observations")   m <- m + tm_shape(neexdzii_fish_obs) +     do.call(tm_symbols, c(fish_args, list(col = fish_sty$mark$color))) }  # Falls — same, straight from the registry if (nrow(neexdzii_falls) > 0) {   falls_args <- gq_tmap_style(reg, "fiss_obstacles")   m <- m + tm_shape(neexdzii_falls) +     do.call(tm_symbols, c(falls_args, list(col = falls_sty$mark$color))) }  # Stream labels if (nrow(stream_labels) > 0) {   m <- m + tm_shape(stream_labels) +     tm_text("gnis_name", size = 0.65, fontface = "italic", col = "#1a5276",             options = opt_tm_text(shadow = TRUE, remove_overlap = TRUE)) }  # Legends from the registry. gq_tmap_legend() partitions by geometry type, # expands classified layers to one entry per class, merges simple and classified # layers of the same type into one legend, and collapses classes that render # identically. `present` cuts road classes to the ones the data actually has. # Salmon habitat is the most prominent linework on this map, and it was absent # from this list until #61 -- the reader saw red dominating the figure with # nothing saying what red meant, while the prose below described its widths and # dashes in detail. Building the legend from the layer list answers "did I list # my layers", which always says yes. The check that catches this is the other # direction: rank what draws the eye in the rendered image, then confirm each of # those is here. # # `present` cuts each classified layer to the classes its data actually carries. # Habitat drops its `;INTERMITTENT` variants too -- they differ from their solid # twins by a dash alone, and carrying all twelve would put eighteen entries in # one box on a figure published about 700 px wide. The dash is explained once in # prose instead. Note this is a narrowing decision, not a collapse: # gq_tmap_legend() keys its dedup on the whole row including the label, so the # repeated colours here do not merge on their own. habitat_classes <- unique(neexdzii_habitat$mapping_code) habitat_legend <- grep(";INTERMITTENT$", habitat_classes,                        value = TRUE, invert = TRUE)  leg <- gq_tmap_legend(   reg,   c("Lake" = "lake", "Wetland" = "wetland", "Stream" = "streams_all",     "streams_salmon",     "roads_dra", "Railway" = "railway",     "crossings_pscis_assessment",     "Fish obs" = "bcfishobs_fiss_fish_observations",     "Falls" = "fiss_obstacles"),   present = list(roads_dra = unique(neexdzii_roads$road_type),                  streams_salmon = habitat_legend,                  crossings_pscis_assessment = unique(                    crossings_assessed$barrier_status)) )  m <- Reduce(`+`, c(list(m), lapply(leg, function(x) do.call(tm_add_legend, x))))  # Layout: four-corner rule -- each element gets a corner of its own. # # The scalebar sat at bottom-CENTRE until #16, which is not a corner: it is the # gap between the bottom-left legend and the bottom-right keymap. That survived # only while the legend was narrow. Once the symbols grew to their true registry # sizes the legend got taller and wider, overlapped the bar and clipped its own # last entry. Top-left was the free corner all along. # - Legend:   bottom-left # - Logo:     top-right # - Scalebar: top-left # - Keymap:   bottom-right (via grid viewport) # # Bottom-left is where "legend over least-important terrain" lands here, and it # was settled by rendering both, not by reasoning. Top-left looks like the # better corner -- the upper band is empty ground outside the AOI -- but a # nineteen-row legend hung from it reaches down over the northwest arm and hides # the barrier crossings, which are the most important points on the map. The # bottom-left box overlaps the southwest arm instead, where nothing is # obscured. Read the PNG; the emptiest corner of the frame is not necessarily # the least important. m <- m + tm_scalebar(   # gq_scale_breaks() needs metre units and says so, so project the bbox first   breaks = gq_scale_breaks(st_bbox(st_transform(st_as_sfc(bbox), 3005))),   text.size = 0.7,   position = c("left", "top"),   margins = c(0, 0, 0, 0) ) + tm_logo(logo_path, position = c("right", "top"), height = 2.5,         margins = c(0, 0, 0, 0)) + tm_layout(   frame = TRUE,   frame.lwd = 0.5,   asp = 0,   legend.position = c("left", "bottom"),   legend.frame = TRUE,   legend.bg.color = "white",   legend.bg.alpha = 0.85,   # Sized for the width the figure is PUBLISHED at, not the width it is   # rendered at. A 7 in figure lands in roughly a 700 px column, so it is scaled   # to about 60% -- text set to look right in the render is a few pixels on the   # page.   legend.text.size = 0.7,   legend.title.size = 0.8,   inner.margins = c(0.001, 0.001, 0.001, 0.001),   outer.margins = c(0.003, 0.003, 0.003, 0.003),   meta.margins = 0 )  # The tile credit goes BELOW the frame: the four corners are taken -- scale # bar, logo, legend, keymap -- and a line under the map collides with none of # them and travels with the image. The map prints into a viewport above a fixed # strip, so it keeps its 7:9 canvas (the figure is 9.25 in tall for that) and # the keymap below nests inside it, placed against the frame rather than the # device. tm_credits(position = tm_pos_out()) was the obvious route; it shrinks # the frame off 7:9, which bands the basemap, and with meta.margins = 0 tmap # 4.2 stops with "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed". strip <- grid::unit(0.25, "inches") map_vp <- grid::viewport(y = 1, just = "top",                          height = grid::unit(1, "npc") - strip) print(m, vp = map_vp) if (!is.null(credit)) {   grid::grid.text(credit, x = grid::unit(0.004, "npc"), y = strip * 0.5,                   just = "left", gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 7, col = "grey30")) } # gq_tmap_keymap() supplies the PLACEMENT here, not the map: it derives the # viewport centre from the corner and margin and sizes it off the canvas aspect, # which is the arithmetic every hand-rolled inset hardcodes. Its own two-layer # map is discarded in favour of `keymap` above, which carries a third layer # (watershed groups) that the (aoi, context) signature cannot express. km <- gq_tmap_keymap(neexdzii_wsd, neexdzii_bc, asp = 7 / 9) grid::pushViewport(map_vp) print(keymap, vp = km$viewport) grid::popViewport()
